```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

## Goal

Creates an Rmd document that is renderd into a PDF with the selected outputs in the application.

- On: `run_app(..., enable_odg = TRUE)`.
- Dataset list needs a `load_fn` attribute: a function with no arguments and independent from its parent environment.
That reproduces the dataset_list from scratch.
- A module can return an entry `to_odg` from its server.

## Document contents

### For users

The download is a zip with the document as a PDF and the files that produced it. The document contains:

- The selected outputs, one section per module, recomputed from the data with the filters and settings in place in the app.
- Where the data comes from: modification dates, a hash per dataset to check it is the data loaded in the app, and the filters applied.
- The session info and any warnings raised while rendering.

### For app creators:

#### `load_fn`

Only the body of `load_fn` is copied into the document, and the document runs in a new R process. So `load_fn` must 
be self-contained, i.e. it must be able to run by itself in a new clean R session, therefore:

- Have no arguments. Not even with defaults.
- Not use its closure: nothing from the environment where it was defined.
- Call package functions with `pkg::`. The document does not attach the packages the app attached with `library()`.

```{r}
# Works: everything the body needs is in the body
attr(data, "load_fn") <- function() {
  list(adsl = haven::read_sas("/data/study/adsl.sas7bdat"))
}

# Fails in the document: `path` only exists where the function was defined
path <- "/data/study/adsl.sas7bdat"
attr(data, "load_fn") <- function() list(adsl = haven::read_sas(path))
```

### For developers

The document is an R Markdown file that rebuilds everything from code: first the data (`load_fn`, subgroups and filter), then one chunk per `to_odg` element. It is rendered in a separate R process, so each element's code must run without the app session. An element that cannot be produced shows an error in its place instead of failing the document.


## What the module server returns

```
server(afmm) returns
└─ list(
     to_odg = list(                       # named, names unique within the module
       <element_name> = list(             # elements appear in this order
         label   = "...",                 # optional: section title, defaults to <element_name>
         info    = "...",                 # optional: defaults to label
         codegen = list(
           pdf = <metareactive | chunk>
         )
       ),
       ...
     )
   )
```

## `codegen` option 1: metareactive

```{r}
listing <- shinymeta::metaReactive(
  {
    adsl <- ..(afmm[["filtered_dataset_list"]]())[["adsl"]]
    adsl[adsl[["AGE"]] > ..(input[["min_age"]]), ]
  },
  varname = "listing"
)

list(
  to_odg = list(
    listing = list(
      label = "Listing",
      codegen = list(pdf = listing)
    )
  )
)
```

## `codegen` option 2: chunk

```{r}
chunk <- structure(
  function(header) {
    paste0(header, "```{r}\nplot(1:10)\n```")
  },
  class = "chunk"
)
```

- A `function(header)` with class `"chunk"` that returns Rmd markup as a single string. The markup is inserted as is.
- `header` is the section title, already formatted as LaTeX and ending in a blank line.

## Precision of the values written into the document

The document is rebuilt from code, so every value taken from the app is written into the Rmd as text. The PDF is
always self-consistent: the code in the Rmd produces exactly the PDF.

- **Data:** reloaded by `load_fn`, never written as text, so it is exact.
- **Filter and subgroups:** written as the JSON text the app received, and parsed by the same function in the app and
  in the document. Range bounds are exact, so the document keeps the same rows as the app.
- **Values a module writes into its code**, with `..()` in a metareactive or with `deparse()`/`deparse1()` in a chunk:
  numbers keep 15 significant digits. A number that needs more is rounded, e.g. `400 / 3` (`133.33333333333334`) is
  written as `133.333333333333`. When such a value is compared with the data, e.g. a threshold equal to a data value,
  the document can keep different rows than the app. Write the number with 17 significant digits to keep it exact:

```{r}
# The document reads `as.numeric("133.33333333333334")`, the same double as in the app
threshold <- as.numeric(..(sprintf("%.17g", input[["threshold"]])))
```

## Chunk labels

Chunk labels must be unique in the document. As convention we reuse the Shiny ids, `<namespace>-<name>`.

- Some chunk labels are assigned by dv.manager. Those lables have the namespace `odg-` (`odg-setup`, `odg-data_source`, ...).
  - No module id can be `odg` or start with `odg-`.
- `<module_id>-`: the module's chunks.
  - metareactive: labelled `<module_id>-<element_name>`. Characters knitr rejects become `_`.
  - chunk: the module labels its own chunks. Every chunk must be labelled using the shiny namespace (`session$ns(NULL)` for a single chunk).
  Any other id that must be unique in the document (e.g. LaTeX link targets) must be labelled and namespaced also.
    - Unlabelled chunks are also an option, knitr numbers them.

## Code formatting with air

The R code in the document is formatted with [air], using the following logic.

1. `options(dv_odg_air_path = "/path/to/air")`
2. environment variable `DV_ODG_AIR_PATH`
3. `air` on the `PATH`
4. Otherwise, unformatted.
